independence.source_review: Read all applicable common/base-faction text, base component inventory, glossary, Fall/Winter and V.1-3 in extracted/root-rules.txt; checked PDF text and visually inspected PDF pages 5 and 10 for setup, icons and Populate Ruins. The source itself, not ledger mappings, determined expected rules. References to earlier reviews inside supplied ledger/corrections were treated only as claims to independently test.

findings.finding: The v8 key says to remove four dominance cards and draw three, but omits the initial shared-deck shuffle explicitly between those steps. The existing broad standard-setup/deck-change request is sufficient scope; complete this key rather than adding another question. Q25 only requests the separate empty-deck shuffle and does not request initial setup randomization.
findings.proposed_answer: Remove all four dominance cards, then shuffle the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Four ruins cover the R slots. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, 2 coins. Factions set up in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. If Vagabond is present, during its faction setup take the four ruins and the R-marked bag, boot, hammer and sword; put one item beneath each ruin, shuffle the ruin/item stacks as instructed, then return each stack to an empty R ruin slot. Without Vagabond, no hidden ruin items are populated.

findings.finding: Accept the documented v8 conditional hidden-item correction. Q07 does not restrict ruins/item setup to common setup alone; faction setup is also explicitly part of its request. With Vagabond present, Populate Ruins is the necessary item-setup procedure: take four ruins and R bag/boot/hammer/sword, one beneath each, shuffle as prescribed, return stacks to empty ruin slots. Without Vagabond, Standard Setup itself supplies no hidden R items. Q35 explicitly excludes hidden ruin items, so it cannot stand in for Q07.

Accept the documented v8 Recruit completion. Asking how the Eyrie resolve the Decree includes actually performing each card action, not only identifying the suit location. Ordinary Recruit is one warrior in one chosen matching roost clearing; Charismatic changes it to two. No separate question or novelty increment is warranted.

Q46 is correct and worth retaining, but not independent new coverage. Q14 already directly asks the complete Outrage triggers and gives warrior movement/removal of sympathy; Q01/Q17 establish the pawn distinction; Q28 establishes forced actions under the affected player's rules. Testing placement, pawn-only entry or allied-warrior entry applies those same trigger words. The allied entry example adds neither an exception nor a new timing/priority rule. The ability to bring allies is separately requested in Q54.
findings.proposed_ledger_change: Move Q46 from accepted additions to retained_regression_only; set counts_as_new_coverage false. Keep the frozen question and its correct answer.

findings.finding: Retain Q56 as qualifying, but narrow its novelty explanation. Broad corrected Q04 already requests crafting costs/repeat use and includes the mixed-suit constraint and repeated-pawn exception. Q56 independently and explicitly requests immediate use of the newly crafted item, supported by 9.2.1 allowing immediate face-up acquisition. That remains its valid distinct hook. Do not count the overlapping cost/repeat details as additional new rules.

No further independent core procedural question is required after completing Q07. The remaining apparent gaps are defaults already requested, retained repetitions, routine consequences, nonprocedural component-aid distribution, or explicit exclusions. The review imposes no question cap or quota.
